title: Not a Feather Out of Place

say.speaker: healer
say.text: Hold still for one second, {name:partner}. You have a scrape right along your left shoulder.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: Forget the shoulder, {name:healer}! Tell me honestly, did that dusty gust flatten my crest?

say.speaker: healer
say.text: You took a direct knock in the mud and the very first thing on your mind is your hairdo?

say.speaker: partner
say.text: It is not vanity! Clean feathers cut the wind cleaner, and sharp footwork starts at the crown.

say.speaker: healer
say.text: Sure it does. Here, hold this crushed Pecha-petal paste against the bruise before it swells.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: Whoa, that cooled down fast. Did you gather those petals back at camp this morning?

say.speaker: healer
say.text: Of course! Someone has to keep a spare salve handy when our proudest dancer forgets to duck.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: Still awake, {name:healer}? The lantern oil is nearly down to the rim, and you are still grinding herbs.

say.speaker: healer
say.text: We burned through half our poultices today. If I steep these clover stems overnight, they set twice as strong.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: Your eyes are drooping, though. Set the mortar down and drink this warm berry tea before it goes cold.

say.speaker: healer
say.text: Mm, sweet and tart. Did you raid the kitchen pot just for me?

say.speaker: partner
say.text: I knew you would still be awake fussing over bandages. You always pack extra for the whole neighborhood.

say.speaker: healer
say.text: If a remedy fails out here, it hurts someone I grew up beside. Making extra batches is the one way I stay ahead of the worry.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: Then give me the spare mortar. Two pairs of hands finish in half the time, and neither of us misses tomorrow's march.

say.speaker: healer
say.text: Do not give me that grin, {name:partner}! You dove straight into a stray rock blast just to block my flank!

say.speaker: partner
say.text: Ouch, easy with the wrap! Look, you were mid-heal, and I was already pivoting that way anyway.

say.speaker: healer
say.text: Liar. You have been throwing yourself ahead of me since we were knee-high in the orchard.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: Can you blame me? Whenever things turn ugly, my head goes blank if I think something might reach you first.

say.speaker: healer
say.text: And what do you think happens to my focus when you hit the dirt in front of me? I am not fragile anymore, {name:partner}.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: I know you are not. Seeing you stand calm in the middle of chaos is half the reason I can keep my footing.

say.speaker: healer
say.text: Good. Then watch your own front, and trust me to guard both our backs from here on out.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: Listen to the crickets once the embers sink low, {name:healer}. Sounds almost like our old garden fence back home.

say.speaker: healer
say.text: Remember how you used to hop up on that crooked post and dare me to race you to the brook before sunrise?

say.speaker: partner
say.text: And I always slipped on the mossy stone so you had to patch my scraped knees with clover leaves before anyone noticed!

say.speaker: healer
say.text: We thought crossing the creek was the farthest adventure in the world. Now look how many miles sit between us and home.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: No matter how wild the road gets ahead, {name:healer}, I never feel lost as long as I hear you right behind my shoulder.

say.speaker: healer
say.text: Then make me one promise, {name:partner}. Not a reckless hero speech, just a real promise.

say.speaker: healer
say.text: When this expedition ends, we walk back through that orchard gate together, both of us whole, just like we left.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: You have my word on it. Step for step on the way out, and step for step all the way home.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: Pivot left, step through, strike! Wait, why did my heel catch on the turn again?!

say.speaker: mentor
say.text: You are throwing your weight ahead of your hips, {name:partner}. Slow the spin down by half and plant your heel first.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: Dad?! How long were you standing by the supply wagon?

say.speaker: mentor
say.text: Long enough to watch you repeat the same Royal Guard drill six times in a row. You have plenty of fire, kiddo.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: When you move in battle, every step lands cleanly without wasting a motion. I still feel clumsy beside you.

say.speaker: mentor
say.text: Every veteran looks effortless after twenty years of bruised toes. Fix that stance and show me one steady step.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: Dad, can I ask something about your Royal Guard days? How did you know you were ready to stand beside the King?

say.speaker: mentor
say.text: Hah! Truth be told, I was terrified my first week in the courtyard. Half the knights towered over me.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: No way! You never look rattled when enemies charge straight at our line.

say.speaker: mentor
say.text: Oh, I still get rattled, {name:partner}. Mostly whenever I see you sprint forward to draw the first hit.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: Wait, really? I only push hard so you do not have to carry the whole front by yourself anymore.

say.speaker: mentor
say.text: I know, son, and I am grateful. Just remember a parent never truly stops fretting, even while cheering loudest from behind.

say.speaker: mentor
say.text: I watched you hold the eastern flank today, {name:partner}. Tight turn, zero wasted energy.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: Really? I thought my second turn came out a little narrower than the old Royal Guard form you taught me.

say.speaker: mentor
say.text: It did, and that is why it worked. My old form belonged to palace flagstones, not muddy trails and sudden ambushes.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: So I do not have to copy every step verbatim?

say.speaker: mentor
say.text: Never. I taught you the rhythm so you could build a stride of your own, and watching you outgrow my shadow makes me prouder than any medal.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: Then keep pace with me out there tomorrow, Dad. Let us see what both our strides can do together.

say.speaker: healer
say.text: Here is your bowl, {name:mentor}! I tossed extra wild thyme in so the camp stew smells a little closer to home.

say.speaker: mentor
say.text: Ah, bless you, {name:healer}. One whiff of thyme takes me straight back to our valley table with your mother.

say.speaker: healer
say.text: Do you miss those loud village dinners? Mom always baked two extra loaves because you and the kids swept the basket clean.

say.speaker: mentor
say.text: Every single evening. Nobody kneads herb bread like Florges, and nobody trades tall tales across the table like our family.

say.speaker: healer
say.text: I bet she is watering the front border right now, waiting for word from us.

say.speaker: mentor
say.text: She knows we will return every last one of you safely to her table. Until then, let us keep her recipe alive on the road.

say.speaker: mentor
say.text: {name:healer}? You should be fast asleep in the tent. Is something wrong?

say.speaker: healer
say.text: Nothing is wrong. I noticed you took the midnight watch for the third night running, so I brought warm chamomile.

say.speaker: mentor
say.text: That is mighty thoughtful of you. An old guard sleeps light anyway, so I might as well let the younger squad rest.

say.speaker: healer
say.text: I never really said thank you properly, {name:mentor}. Back in the village, and out here too, you always step between us and trouble.

say.speaker: mentor
say.text: Raising you kids alongside Florges gave this soldier a real home again. Guarding you is never a chore.

say.speaker: healer
say.text: Still, let us share the quiet for ten minutes before I head back. Even a Royal Guard deserves someone looking out for him.

say.speaker: pawmi
say.text: Hey, {name:partner}! Ready for round two after that wild scrimmage back on the hometown pitch?

say.speaker: partner
say.text: Hey! The grass was slick with evening dew, and I was mid-turn! You caught me flat-footed with that cheap sidestep!

say.speaker: pawmi
say.text: Haha, an excuse for every weather report! Admit it, you never saw my cheek pouches light up until I dashed straight past your guard.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: Fine, you scored the opener! Put your pads up after mess call, {name:pawmi}. No way I am letting that count as the final tally.

say.speaker: pawmi
say.text: Now you are talking! Just try not to let those sparks ruffle your precious crest.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: Save the jokes for after you try landing a second hit on me!

say.speaker: pawmi
say.text: Whoa! You slipped right under my left jab before the spark even crackled!

say.speaker: partner
say.text: Counted your shoulder dip! Your fur puffs up half a heartbeat before you lunge with Nuzzle.

say.speaker: pawmi
say.text: Wait, really? Nobody back in town ever read that windup before.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: I have spent weeks practicing side-steps so electric foes cannot pin me down again. You make a brutal sparring partner.

say.speaker: pawmi
say.text: Then I have to hide my tell, do I? Good! Fighting someone who reads my tricks forces me to get faster too.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: Catch your breath for ten seconds and go again! Next round, I am closing the distance before you blink.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: That cross-step today was slick, {name:pawmi}. You shut down that flank rush before I even finished pivoting.

say.speaker: pawmi
say.text: Took a cue from your footwork! Watching you weave through heavy hitters made me stop lunging straight ahead.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: Wait, you were studying my drills? I thought you only joined the road to settle our pitch score.

say.speaker: pawmi
say.text: Half of it was pride, sure. The other half was hearing how wild the Rift got and refusing to sit home while you marched into it.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: Having your sparks covering my blind side beats any solo rematch, {name:pawmi}. Nobody keeps me sharper than you.

say.speaker: pawmi
say.text: Deal! We keep the hometown banner flying out front, and save the tiebreaker match for the victory feast!

say.speaker: caterpie
say.text: Look at how clean this morning dew sits on the clover, {name:healer}. Every drop catches the sunrise like tiny glass beads.

say.speaker: healer
say.text: Most of the squad stomps right past without looking down. You always find the prettiest corners of every trail, {name:caterpie}.

say.speaker: caterpie
say.text: Does dew taste different out here in the hills compared to our village meadow?

say.speaker: healer
say.text: Taste a drop from the mint leaf beside you! Mountain mist leaves a crisp tang that valley grass never gets.

say.speaker: caterpie
say.text: Whoa, it really does! Fresh and cool, like cold spring water.

say.speaker: healer
say.text: Next rest stop, let us scout the sunny ridges together before camp wakes up.

say.speaker: caterpie
say.text: Excuse me, {name:healer}? I found this tiny pale blossom tucked under a mossy stone. Could its leaves help your salves?

say.speaker: healer
say.text: Oh! That is silver-bell bloom! It rarely grows near dusty roads because travelers trample the shoots.

say.speaker: caterpie
say.text: I was careful! I pinched only two outer petals and left the stem and roots untouched.

say.speaker: healer
say.text: You treated it like a seasoned herbalist! Watch what happens when we dab the sap onto this scratched leaf.

say.speaker: caterpie
say.text: The edges knitted right back together! I always wondered how you kept our satchels smelling so fresh.

say.speaker: healer
say.text: Keep those sharp eyes on the hedgerows, {name:caterpie}. Nobody else in camp spots quiet gifts like you do.

say.speaker: caterpie
say.text: {name:healer}, do you ever feel small out here? Everyone else hits like thunder, and I mostly tangle foes up or hide in tall grass.

say.speaker: healer
say.text: Small? Wait a minute, think about that silver-bell flower you found clinging to bare rock last week.

say.speaker: caterpie
say.text: The tiny pale one? What about it?

say.speaker: healer
say.text: Storms tear down giant oaks, yet wildflowers bend with the wind and push steady roots right through cracked stone.

say.speaker: caterpie
say.text: So slowing an enemy down or spotting a safe path really does count for something?

say.speaker: healer
say.text: More than you know. Every time you pause to notice the world around us, you keep the rest of us from losing our gentle hearts on the march.

say.speaker: caterpie
say.text: Thank you, {name:healer}. I will keep watching the quiet ground ahead so you always have petals ready for the fight.
